question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European Fortifications in India]
options: Fort William — British stronghold at Calcutta (Bengal)
Fort St. George — British administrative and military base at Madras
Fort Geldria — Dutch East India Company's fortified post at Pulicat
Fort St. Angelo — French military headquarters built at Pondicherry
wrong_fact: Fort St. Angelo is located in Kannur (Cannanore), Kerala, and was built by the Portuguese in 1505. The primary French fort in Pondicherry was Fort Louis.
explanation: Fort William was constructed by the British in Calcutta. Fort St. George was the first English fortress in India, founded at Madras in 1644. Fort Geldria was established by the Dutch in Pulicat in 1613. Fort St. Angelo was built by Francisco de Almeida, the first Portuguese Viceroy, in Kannur.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Introduction of European Military Systems]
options: Battle of Adyar (1746) — Demonstrated the superiority of small, disciplined European-trained forces over a larger Indian army
Cartaz System — Portuguese naval licensing system enforcing maritime monopoly in the Indian Ocean
Sepoy System — Recruitment of native Indian soldiers trained in European infantry tactics and drill
Flintlock Musket — Introduced by the Marathas to capture Portuguese Vasai in 1540
wrong_fact: The Marathas captured Vasai (Bassein) from the Portuguese in 1739 (not 1540) under Chimaji Appa. In 1540, the Marathas did not even exist as a unified military power, and matchlock/flintlock weapons were not used in this way.
explanation: The Battle of Adyar (1746) proved that a small French-trained force under Paradis could defeat the large cavalry army of Nawab Anwar-ud-din. The Cartaz system forced merchant ships to pay duties and carry passes. The sepoy system was adopted by the French and British, creating disciplined standing infantry. The Maratha siege of Vasai in 1739 was a notable military success, but occurred in the 18th century.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Naval Bases and Marine Technology]
options: Bombay Dockyard — Established in 1735 by the Wadia family, constructing teak-hulled ships for the Royal Navy
Anjediva Island — Portuguese fortified naval base off the coast of Karnataka used to intercept Malabar trade
Negapatam — Dutch naval stronghold captured by the British during the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War
Sadras — Danish shipyard specializing in copper-sheathing of ironclads on the Coromandel Coast
wrong_fact: Sadras was a Dutch factory and fort (Fort Sadras) on the Coromandel Coast, not Danish. Copper-sheathed ironclad steamships belong to the mid-19th century and were not built there.
explanation: The Wadia shipbuilders in Bombay established a world-class dockyard in 1735, building ships that were more durable than British oak. Anjediva Island was fortified by Almeida in 1505 for naval dominance. Negapatam was the chief Dutch base on the Coromandel coast before its capture by the British in 1781. Sadras was famous for its Dutch-woven muslin, not a Danish shipyard.
